target_customer: Professional ticket brokers and season ticket holders who resell tickets
problem: Most resale is manual: spreadsheets, guessed prices and listing one marketplace at a time, with big brokers outsourcing pricing to offshore teams.
business_model: Marketplace-style take rate of 10 percent per ticket sold, with automated pricing, listing and distribution software
product_category: Ticket resale automation (AI pricing and multi-marketplace distribution)

founders.name: Truman Gelnovatch
founders.background_notes: YC page says he has flipped tickets for about five years and met his co-founder on Princeton's men's soccer team.

founders.name: Ryan Clare
education: Princeton, computer science with machine learning focus
founders.background_notes: Company long description says he built pricing software after seeing the mess first-hand.

technical_complexity.rationale: Repricing, barcode and account import, delivery transfer and payouts across 8+ marketplaces is integration-heavy but standard engineering; marketplace API access is the hard part.

defensibility.rationale: Many broker tools already offered repricing, so the differentiator is distribution to season ticket holders and execution; inventory connections give modest lock-in.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Search results showed Ticketmaster shutting down its TradeDesk broker platform in 2025, but no copy or purchase of Ticket Wallet was found.

market_need_then: The company states resale is a $26B market and that brokers price by hand or outsource it; its site later claims 3,000+ active sellers and $18M+ in tickets sold, which is self-reported.

identity.logo: not described by any opened source
identity.voice_and_tone: Direct, confident and results-focused; a line is We didn't study this market. We lived in it.

brand_strength.rationale: The name describes a generic category and collides with Apple Wallet style ticket wallet products; no press about the brand itself was found.

outcome_analysis: Ticket Wallet is active and growing after Spring 2025. A CEO who resold tickets for years paired with a machine learning co-founder, launched a take-rate product, and reportedly raised a $6M seed in July 2025 led by Seven Seven Six. Team size reached about 20. Traction numbers are self-reported. Risks are marketplace access and rules on resale, but no failure signals were found.
notes: The $6M seed is reported by SeedTable and Signalbase, both aggregators, and by a LinkedIn post per a search summary; no Form D or press release was found. Caplight lists $500K from April 2025 with Pioneer Fund, 776 and YC, which looks like the pre-batch or YC stage. Outcome search returned only other ticketing companies. Competitor search returned undated vendor blog lists, so no dated competitors are recorded. Founder prior employers not found.
